title: Manchester United's revolving dugout is costing a fortune
body:
Manchester United's managerial merry-go-round now runs close to £100m in total [S1]. After sacking Michael Carrick, they moved to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as head coach [S2]. The dugout has become a revolving door, and the bill is the uncomfortable headline.

The detail that stands out is the speed of the money. United borrowed £10m just three days after confirming Pochettino as their new head coach [S1]. That borrowing comes alongside a £7.5m compensation payment to US Soccer [S1]. Sky Sports presented the appointment as a straightforward announcement [S2], but the financial trail tells a messier story.

The results explain the urgency. Over their last five league games, they have won none, drawn three and lost two, collecting 3 points [ST1]. They have scored 6 and conceded 11, with the sequence reading DDLLD [ST1]. Those figures show a side leaking goals and short of belief.

Every board loves a fresh start, and every fan just wants a plan that survives a bad month. The sack is the easiest lever to pull and the hardest one to get right.

The Touchline Take: get the next appointment right and this whole expensive saga gets forgotten.
